note: Process and vintage only. No disruption count, score or rank appears here, because reporting environments differ too much for those to be compared between countries.

lanes.source_family: Public Safety Canada, Canadian Disaster Database: the Open Government extract (newest edition) and the legacy CDD search interface
lanes.limitation: Carried forward. The publisher has issued no edition after the 2022 extract, so 2023-2026 is absent from the source, not unsearched. The xlsx was not re-downloaded (the site firewall refused a scripted client in iteration 17; not retried), so 'no newer edition' rests on the dataset page's resource list and modified date.
lanes.finding: Nothing new published since iteration 17. The 13 in-window events of the 2022 extract keep their iteration-16 dispositions.

lanes.source_family: NERC State of Reliability reports and NERC event-analysis reports naming a Canadian entity
lanes.limitation: Carried forward. No State of Reliability covering 2026 operations exists yet, and no event report on a 2026 event naming a Canadian entity has been published; the documents were not re-read this pass because the listings are unchanged.
lanes.finding: Nothing new published since iteration 17. Two 2026 events found under CG3 (British Columbia, 8 March; Alberta, 25 May) would be expected in the next SOR.

lanes.source_family: Operator grid records: AESO EEA/Grid Alert history file and Annual Market Statistics; IESO news-release archive and emergency notice feeds; Hydro-Québec press-r
lanes.limitation: None of the three declared 2026 queries ran (shared search budget exhausted before this agent's first search). Unread: AESO July-November 2026 (MSA Q3 report not yet released), IESO before 2026-08-08 (rolling 90-day archive, no ordinary-access history), IESO and Hydro-Québec annual reports, and the Régie de l'énergie filing behind Hydro-Québec's 2025 distribution report, which may list major events.
lanes.finding: The MSA quarterly reports are a standing substitute for the alert list AESO stopped publishing, with a lag of about six weeks after quarter end; they also record out-of-province events that touched Alberta (the 8 March 2026 British Columbia event came from there). The IESO feed keeps 90 days: unless harvested at least that often its notices are lost (the 2 November 2026 notice ages out in early February 2027).

lanes.source_family: Environment and Climate Change Canada top-ten weather stories (2022-2025 editions), with a utility peak sought for each held story
lanes.limitation: No 2026 ECCC edition exists, so 2026 is outside the census source; 2026 coverage is three utility archives read in part, and no search ran. A 2026 storm at a utility not read, or one the utility issued no release for, would not be found.
lanes.finding: BC Hydro publishes a peak-at-one-time figure alongside its cumulative totals (135,000 at one time against 380,000 to 415,000 cumulative for the November 2026 storms); the cumulative figure is about three times the peak and must not be used.

lanes.source_family: CER pipeline-incident comprehensive CSV (newest edition, served Last-Modified 2026-11-01, open.canada.ca metadata modified 2026-11-02; latest reported date in f
lanes.limitation: The TSB half is an index, not a reading: report bodies and the occurrence dataset are served only from tsb.gc.ca (HTTP 403 on every address tried), and it is unknown whether the portal lists every TSB pipeline investigation. The CER file has not been refreshed since 2026-11-01 and stops at 2026-10-22. Nine interruption rows remain held with no public report opened, because the lane declares no queries and search was unavailable.
lanes.finding: The CER interruption flag is still undefined beyond its one-line dictionary entry, and nothing opened in three passes shows that a 'short-term interruption' flag corresponds to a reported shutdown. Suggest the lead rule that the flag alone never meets clause 3.

lanes.source_family: Declared query set (plan A.1) over refineries, upgraders and gas plants, each query run once per year 2022-2026; opened pages from the results.
lanes.limitation: The declared set ran through 2026-11-03. An additional 2026 re-check query could not be run in this pass.

lanes.source_family: Declared query set (plan A.1): wildfire/weather production shut-ins with a stated volume in Alberta, BC, Saskatchewan; opened pages from the results. No AER or
lanes.limitation: One declared query (2025, second string) was never run and the 2026 re-run did not happen, so search coverage of June-November 2026 rests on three fetched pages, not on queries. The authority and operator half is thin: AER's media centre was read only for May-November 2026 (3 of about 45 listing pages; 2022-2025 unread), BC Energy Regulator page 1 of 53 only, Saskatchewan's news search returned nothing relevant and was not enumerated, and Suncor (403) and Cenovus (script-only) release archives could not be read. BC and Saskatchewan shut-ins were not searched in substance: both declared strings name Alberta or the oil sands.
lanes.finding: No new event. Every volume-bearing result for 2023 and 2025 resolves to the two Alberta records already in the corpus; 2024 yields only Firebag, for which no opened page states a shut-in volume (215,000 bpd is the site's size). The AER media-centre items read (May-November 2026) contain no wildfire or shut-in announcement, and Alberta's season-end release of 2026-11-02 reports a quiet 2026 season (785 fires, under 18,000 ha) with no mention of energy impacts; neither is proof of absence. Published shut-in volumes in this lane come from operator statements relayed by wire services and from analyst tallies, not from the regulator or provincial pages opened. The declared strings cannot surface BC or Saskatchewan events; a re-run should add province-specific strings.

lanes.source_family: Per-terminal query set (plan A.1) for LNG Canada, Westridge, Canaport, RIPET, Pembina Prince Rupert, Whiffen Head; operator news pages by direct fetch.
lanes.limitation: Pembina Prince Rupert had one general (variant) query and no year queries; Whiffen Head 2022 and 2023 were not run; RIPET and Canaport year queries ran as written but the bare tokens matched unrelated subjects, so those years are run-but-uninformative rather than searched in substance. No operator release archive, CER listing or provincial source was enumerated (LNG Canada's news page refuses automated access), so the lane rests on news search alone.
lanes.finding: The plan's bare terminal tokens do not work as search strings: "RIPET" resolves to the RIPE NCC internet registry, "Westridge" to place names, "Canaport" to general Canadian port news. Both accepted candidates surfaced only under full facility names. A re-run should declare full-name strings ("Ridley Island Propane Export Terminal", "Westridge Marine Terminal", "Saint John LNG" / "Canaport LNG", "Newfoundland Transshipment"). Canaport was renamed Saint John LNG, and that name was not searched. Incidental, outside CL1's universe and not examined: results repeatedly showed a fire at Westshore Terminals (coal, British Columbia) on 16 Aug 2025 closing a berth for about ten weeks.

lanes.source_family: National statistics: NBS monthly energy production releases (能源生产情况), read for production effects explicitly attributed to a disruption
lanes.limitation: Nothing in the universe is unread, but each page was read through WebFetch, which returns a model's reading of the page rather than the raw text; the model declined to reproduce full bodies, so the per-release result rests on its answer to a fixed question asking for every causal phrase verbatim. The attached Excel data tables were not opened. The October 2026 release is not yet published.
lanes.finding: Substantive negative finding: across all 53 releases (data months 2021-12 to 2026-09) the NBS energy production release never attributes a production change to a disruption. No release mentions an accident, flood, typhoon, drought or water inflow, weather, shutdown, power rationing, or maintenance, and no release gives a province-level figure: all figures are national totals for above-scale industry. The only causal wording found is supply-policy language attached to coal growth in six releases (data months 2021-12, 2022-03, 2022-04, 2022-05, 2022-06, 2022-11: for example 增产保供政策持续推进, 煤炭保供稳价政策深入推进, 为做好今冬保暖保供工作), plus a days-adjustment phrase for power generation (扣除天数原因) in data months 2025-03 to 2025-08 and a recurring comparability footnote. From 2022-12 onward the text is purely descriptive. Large swings are reported with no stated cause, for example hydro generation -30.0% in 2022-09, -32.9% in 2023-05 and -22.9% for the first half of 2023. This source family therefore cannot yield candidates under any clause, and an unexplained change in it must not be read as evidence of a disruption.

lanes.source_family: National Energy Administration and grid companies (State Grid, China Southern Grid): notices of major outages, orderly power use, emergency responses
lanes.limitation: State Grid's site did not respond and NEA's general news listing is script-only, so both are unread; China Southern Grid's company-news archive is reachable (20 items a page, paged as index_N.html, by year) but only 3 pages (60 titles) were sampled, and none of the 15 year queries ran before the shared search limit was hit. No English query is declared in the plan and none was run, so the zh+en requirement is not met.
lanes.finding: The NEA safety department's own listing is the one fully read source here and it is almost silent on events: of 275 titles in the window, 3 concern an actual outage (Gansu earthquake Dec 2023, two items; Hebei Zhuozhou floods Aug 2023) and 1 names an event (Xinjiang 3 Aug 2024 oscillation) without stating any effect. The monthly 事故通报 and 全国电力安全生产情况 series on that listing stop in 2021 (last: Oct 2021 data, published 2021-11-30); nothing in the window replaces them. The site: operator is ignored by the search tool; allowed_domains works for nea.gov.cn, csg.cn and sgcc.com.cn and returned operator pages. Planned demand management seen and logged apart, not as candidates: none on NEA/CSG/SGCC pages in this lane.

lanes.source_family: Provincial outage and disruption reporting: provincial energy bureaus and government notices of power rationing or grid emergencies
lanes.limitation: A declared query set, not a census: each query returned about 10 results and only 5 result pages were opened; provincial energy-bureau notice listings were not enumerated. The 'P 大面积停电 应急响应 政府' query returns emergency plans (预案) for almost every province, often from other provinces, and is a poor instrument for finding events.
lanes.finding: Yield was plans, not disruptions. Logged apart as planned demand management or standing rules, never as candidates: Guangzhou 2026 load-management plan and 2021 orderly-power-use plan; Laizhou (Shandong) 2026 summer load-management plan; Inner Mongolia Mengxi/Mengdong orderly-power-use plans (2021, 2022, 2023 editions) and league-level plans; Xinjiang load-management rules (2024); Jiangsu 2024 load-management notice and 2026 electricity-saving notice; Zhejiang 2019 plan; Henan 2020 plan and 2022 supply notice. Provincial NEA office pages migrated in 2023 carry 2023 dates in their URLs but describe older events (Henan Jan 2018, Zhejiang summer 2013); the search summary presented the Zhejiang 2013 event as 2023. Any record built from these subdomains needs the on-page date. One result surfaced for Inner Mongolia was the 2023 Alxa mine collapse already in the corpus (not a grid event, not counted as a candidate).

lanes.source_family: Major state enterprises (Sinopec, PetroChina, CNOOC, China Shenhua, State Power Investment): HKEX and SSE announcements of facility incidents or production susp
lanes.limitation: The notice archives themselves were not enumerated: HKEX and SSE listings are interactive or script-only, and of the five company notice pages only PetroChina's was reachable, showing its 20 most recent titles (2026-04-29 to 2026-11-05, all routine governance, none about a suspension) with no visible pagination. Annual-report PDFs were not opened. All 15 declared queries ran in both languages, but they are a keyword probe of an archive lane, not a reading of it.
lanes.finding: The generic declared queries return mainly pre-2022 events, planned maintenance and share-trading halts (停牌), which the search engine conflates with 停产. No accepted candidate. Two held: CNOOC Lingshui 17-2 field shutdown in 2026 (no volume, no event date) and Guodian Power's Chahasu coal mine regulatory halt, 2023 (filing opened). Unopened leads not made into candidates because no date or page could be read: a report that Sinopec cut refining runs during a Strait of Hormuz crude-supply disruption in 2026 (tankterminals page 404; a supply-driven run cut, lead should decide whether clause 1 can apply at all); unplanned petrochemical-unit stops at Sinopec Qilu (Dec 2023) and PetroChina Liaoyang (Feb 2024), which are chemical units, not refining throughput. The miningweekly 2023-05-09 '50Mt halted' item (403) is probably the aftermath of the Alxa collapse already in the corpus; unverified.

lanes.source_family: Credible Chinese-language media: Xinhua, People's Daily, Caixin, The Paper
lanes.limitation: A 15-string query set through a general search engine is not a search of the four outlets' archives: Caixin returned no result in any of the 18 searches and People's Daily only a handful, so lane credit rests almost entirely on The Paper and Xinhua. No outlet site search was run, and named-event follow-ups (Zhenhai January 2025, held in pass 17) were not possible within the cap.
lanes.finding: No new qualifying event. Plain refinery queries return foreign refineries almost exclusively; domain-restricted reruns return Xinhua world-desk copy on foreign refineries plus the three domestic events already in the corpus. Coal queries return a recurring pattern in The Paper: listed-company notices of single-mine halts after one-fatality accidents, stating approved capacity but no lost volume (the one stated loss was about 90,000 t). Gas-pipeline queries return only urban distribution incidents (Yanjiao 2024, Anping 2023) and events outside the window (Shiyan 2021, Qinglong) or outside China; no domestic trunk-pipeline shutdown surfaced. 'examined' is an approximate count of result items across 18 searches.

lanes.source_family: International corroboration: Reuters, Bloomberg, S&P Global reporting of Chinese energy disruptions
lanes.limitation: All 15 declared English queries ran and were dispositioned, but this is a query set, not a census, and the wire syndication sites carrying most Reuters and Bloomberg coal stories (mining.com, miningweekly, engineeringnews) refused access, so those articles were judged from headlines. Three held candidates had no Chinese-language follow-up because the 22-search cap was reached. Seen in result lists and not pursued: 2024 Shanxi safety-inspection output curbs (a regulatory campaign, not a discrete event), two mine accidents of 23 Oct 2024 in Hebei and Shanxi, and a reported 2024 output fall in one Heilongjiang city.
lanes.finding: English wire coverage of Chinese power rationing found no firm load shed after 2023: results for 2024, 2025 and 2026 report record demand and renewable curtailment, not rationing. English refinery-fire coverage for 2022-2026 returned only events already in the corpus plus one commissioning fire and one walled headline. Coal-accident coverage is dense but almost never states a supply cut in tonnes; trade press (Mysteel) states halted capacity, behind a login wall.

lanes.source_family: Grid-India (formerly POSOCO) and CEA grid-disturbance / grid-incident reports
lanes.limitation: The Grid-India/RLDC universe is unread for the whole window 2022-01-01 to 2026-11-10: all six hosts refused the connection for the third pass running. No RPC, parliamentary or ministry document was opened either (refused, HTTP 403 or script-only), so no event-level alternative was read.
lanes.finding: CEA publishes no grid-disturbance event listing or count: its Annual Report 2025-26 has none and its division pages carry only the procedure. That procedure places the register and the categorisation with the RLDCs; RPC papers are a downstream discussion copy, per region, at station level, and count MW not customers. No proxy is recommended; see IN1_ALTERNATIVES.md.

lanes.source_family: Ministry of Power releases (pib.gov.in) on major outages and supply emergencies
lanes.limitation: Nothing in this lane was read. Every PIB endpoint tried (listing, RSS, a release page) and the Ministry of Power site returned HTTP 403 to ordinary fetches, and the five declared queries were refused by the shared search budget. The whole universe, 2022-01-01 to 2026-11-10, remains unsearched.
lanes.finding: PIB refuses automated ordinary access outright (three distinct endpoints, including its RSS feed). This lane cannot be enumerated by fetch; it needs a person in a browser or a different legitimately published mirror.

lanes.source_family: PPAC / MoPNG refinery and pipeline disruption statements (via the plan's media queries)
lanes.limitation: Unread: PIB-MoPNG releases (403); the MoPNG Monthly Cabinet Summaries (44 listed, February 2021 to September 2024, image-only scans; 1 fetched, none read); PPAC's report archive (300+ entries listed, 1 monthly report read); MoPNG What's New pages 2-6 of 6. Monthly Production Reports for October 2022 and July 2024 are missing from the ministry's listing.
lanes.finding: The MoPNG Monthly Production Report is the only source reached in this lane that attributes refinery throughput changes to causes, and only at month level with no event dates. It stopped doing so: the last refinery-wise reason appears in the June 2024 report; from August 2024 to July 2026 the reports give no refinery reasons even when throughput is below target (October 2024, CPSE refineries 6.70% under target; April 2026, private and JV refineries 17.34% under target; both unexplained). It also passes over some shortfalls: the December 2023 report shows CPCL 14.57% below the prior year with no reason given. PPAC's monthly report is aggregate and gives no causes. MoPNG What's New (page 1 of 6) is regulatory notices only. Upstream sections still give causes through July 2026, without volumes.

lanes.source_family: Ministry of Coal and Coal India: mine accidents and production suspensions (via the plan's media query)
lanes.limitation: Unread: Ministry of Coal releases before 13 November 2025; 31 of 35 in-window Monthly Summaries (none is published after February 2025, and October to December 2023 are missing from the listing); Coal India annual reports and subsidiary reports (script-only listing); the ministry's Accident Portal page; PIB. The DGMS, which holds mine-accident records, is outside this lane's named sources.
lanes.finding: None of the official coal sources reached names an individual mine event. Coal India's press releases are output and offtake announcements; the Monthly Summary for the Cabinet has a fixed format (production, dispatch, auctions, drilling, NLC performance) with no incident or cause section; the annual-report safety chapters give aggregate accident statistics and safety programmes, not dated events or production suspensions; the ministry's Safety Statistics page covers NLCIL only, to November 2022. An empty result here says these sources do not report such events, not that none occurred.

lanes.source_family: PNGRB: gas pipeline incidents and supply interruptions
lanes.limitation: Listings were read at TITLE level only (480 notices, 75 press releases, 54 case studies, 21 incident analyses, 9 reports); just 4 PNGRB PDFs were opened, so an incident mentioned only inside a document body is unseen. Not read: PNGRB annual reports (not found on the site), the orders/complaints-disputes listing (146 feed items), the monthly data-bank NGPL MIS reports, the 2026 Statistical Booklet, 38 of 40 anonymised case studies, and the Oct 2026 High-Level Expert Committee report on pipeline supply security (deliberately not opened: its subject is network resilience, which the scope boundary forbids collecting).
lanes.finding: PNGRB does not publish an incident or emergency notice stream. Its public notices over 2022-2026 are regulatory consultations and authorisations; none announces a pipeline shutdown or force majeure on a line (the 2024 'Force Majeure' notices are claim formats for city-gas licence obligations). Named investigation reports stop at March 2022 (latest incident covered: Dec 2021). From 2025 it publishes anonymised 'Case Studies on Major Incidents' with no date, place or operator (2 of 40 opened, both anonymised; one title prints the date as xx.xx.xxxx), unusable for records. The one dated, named incident list found is Annexure-A of the 6 March 2026 press release: five pipeline incidents between 10 Aug and 30 Nov 2025. The listing pages are script-populated; whether reading the publisher's own data files counts as an alternative endpoint or as working around a script-only page is for the lead to rule (if the latter, this lane is not_started/inaccessible and the five candidates rest on the directly fetched press-release PDF, which the declared search could also have surfaced).

lanes.source_family: State SLDC and discom notices of load shedding or major outages
lanes.limitation: Only 16 of 34 declared queries ran (all 10 year queries in English and Hindi, and the Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra and Tamil Nadu pairs) before the session's shared search limit stopped the pass; the Karnataka, Delhi, Bihar, Jharkhand, Punjab, Haryana, Rajasthan, West Bengal and Assam pairs and both follow-ups did not run. No SLDC or discom notice was opened: Maharashtra SLDC report addresses returned 404, its report lists are script-only, its 2025 disturbance compendium exceeds the fetch size limit, and the Delhi SLDC site refused the connection, so every opened source is press.
lanes.finding: The Hindi query form with a year and no place name returns mostly foreign grid failures (Bangladesh, Pakistan, Nigeria) and little about India; with a state name it returns hours-of-supply complaints. Press reports of load shedding almost never give a customer count; where a figure exists it is an MW deficit or an MW of load shed. Supply-shortfall causes recur in this lane: coal (Maharashtra April 2022, Uttar Pradesh September 2026), low hydro storage and purchased power (Kerala September 2026) and low wind output (Tamil Nadu September 2026). 'examined' counts the result links returned by the 16 searches.

lanes.source_family: Credible national media (PTI, The Hindu, Indian Express, Times of India, Mint) via search
lanes.limitation: None of the five credited outlets was searched or read: the search tool refuses all five domains to its user agent, and that refusal was not worked around. The lane universe is therefore entirely unread for 2022-01-01 to 2026-11-10; the unrestricted discovery run earns no lane credit and left one declared string (refinery 2026) unrun.
lanes.finding: Fuel-supply shortfall as a stated outage cause, counts only, no cause added. Pages opened and in window that concern power supply: 2 (BigMint 2026-05-04; Down To Earth 2026-04-30); pages among them stating a fuel-supply shortfall as the cause of an outage: 0 (BigMint attributes Chandrapur to tube leakage and mentions coal supply only as a recommendation; Down To Earth attributes outage capacity largely to maintenance). Unopened search-result snippets asserting a fuel-supply cause: 3 (April 2022, CEA figure of 7,295 MW of coal plant under outage for fuel shortage, S&P page HTTP 403; June 2026 Maharashtra load shedding linked to coal constraints/quality, page HTTP 403, already a held record; 2026 gas-shortage report on deferred maintenance, not opened). One opened page asserting about 12 GW shut for want of coal and gas is dated 2018 and is outside the window. So the category recurs in headlines for 2022 and 2026 but this lane read no in-window page that states it; the evidence here is snippet-level and must not be counted as read. Separately: the lane as declared cannot be executed with this search tool at all; the lead must decide whether IN7 is re-scoped to reachable outlets or recorded as inaccessible.

lanes.source_family: Ministry of Energy statements as carried by SPA (spa.gov.sa; moenergy.gov.sa), reached through Saudi outlets republishing them
lanes.limitation: Nothing was searched or read in this pass: all ten declared queries were refused by the shared search limit (five attempted, none performed), and SPA (HTTP 403) and the ministry site (no response) refused ordinary access once each. The four English year queries for 2022-2025 have still never been run in any pass.
lanes.finding: SPA search and index pages returned HTTP 403 to ordinary access in this pass, so whether they are script-rendered could not be observed (iteration 17 saw a script-rendered shell at the same search address). No circumvention was attempted.

lanes.source_family: Saudi Aramco disclosures: Tadawul announcements; aramco.com news and annual-report incident statements
lanes.limitation: The Tadawul announcement list refused access (HTTP 403) and was not read; neither declared query ran (shared search limit); the Arabic annual reports were not read (English editions only). Aramco's 2026 interim reports and results releases were deliberately not opened: they are outside the declared 2022-2025 annual-report universe and would carry current operating information during the active campaign.
lanes.finding: All four annual reports (FY2022-FY2025) were read in English. Their only in-window incident-occurrence statement is one risk-factor sentence, repeated each year: a storage facility in Jeddah was attacked in March 2022, with no effect stated. The FY2022 report's committee section also mentions a security-related incident at the North Jeddah Bulk Plant, undated and without effect. No report mentions the March 2022 YASREF event already in the corpus, or any fire, unplanned shutdown, force majeure or production shut-in in 2022-2025. The other dated incidents named are outside the window (2019, 2021). The FY2025 report's events-after-the-reporting-period note lists only financing and a share repurchase. Aramco annual reports are therefore not an incident source for this window.

lanes.source_family: GASTAT and JODI production releases (production effects explicitly attributed to a disruption)
lanes.limitation: Only two monthly IPI release PDFs were read in full (March and April 2026, English), so no continuous span is covered and covered_through is null. The 2022-2025 monthly releases, the Arabic editions and GASTAT's petroleum-and-gas statistics were not read, and the search listing did not show a complete 2022-2025 series on the pages opened. JODI's Saudi metadata page was not reached.
lanes.finding: GASTAT does not attribute production changes to a disruption in the releases read. The monthly IPI release is a short bulletin of index movements: it says the index moved 'affected by the decline in mining and quarrying activity' and names the manufacturing sub-activities that moved, but gives no cause for the mining or refining movement (no incident, attack, outage or policy reason) in the two campaign-period months read. JODI-Oil publishes a numeric database with definitions, a manual and availability footnotes only; the pages opened carry no narrative attribution. A numeric series with no attribution cannot produce an incident, so this lane yields context at most and no candidate.

lanes.source_family: OPEC Monthly Oil Market Report archive
lanes.limitation: All three official OPEC addresses tried (current page, the MOMR download host, the legacy publications page) refused automated access with HTTP 402. No issue was read and no workaround was attempted; the lane needs a person to open the PDFs in a browser.

lanes.source_family: International and regional reporting (Reuters, Bloomberg, AP, S&P Global, Argus, as carried by open outlets), via search
lanes.limitation: Only the 2022 and 2023 query combinations ran (10 of 25, both languages); the shared session search limit refused the 2024 set and prevented 2025 and 2026 entirely, and no follow-up search ran. The three held outage candidates (July 2024, January 2025, December 2025) surfaced incidentally from the 2022-2023 queries and each lacks a customer or MW figure that a named follow-up search might supply.
lanes.finding: No new qualifying event for 2022-2023. English and Arabic refinery and attack queries for those years return the March 2022 attacks (only YASREF, already in the corpus, has a reported effect; the Riyadh refinery statement expressly reports none) and 2026 campaign events already in the corpus; nothing dated 2023. Saudi outage reporting found gives regulator actions and causes but customer counts are absent, and one figure is in residents, so clause 5 could not be shown met. 'examined' is an approximate count of result items across the 10 searches. One search result (a Wikipedia mirror of the 2022 Jeddah article) carried embedded text addressed to the reader's software; it was ignored and the page was not opened.

lanes.source_family: DOE Form OE-417 electric emergency incident and disturbance annual summaries, doe417.pnnl.gov/summaries (the DOE-417 portal's 'Annual Summaries Archives').
lanes.limitation: DOE has published no 2026 OE-417 file as of 2026-11-10 (the three 2026 file names return the portal's HTML shell; server Last-Modified is still 2026-10-08), so 2026-01-01 to 2026-11-10 cannot be enumerated from this source. The execution value restates iteration 17's finding in the two-dimension vocabulary (every published row read; the gap is the publisher's); it is not new coverage, and the 2025 file was verified by size and date header, not re-read.
lanes.finding: DOE publishes OE-417 rows only as annual summaries; the 2026 rows may not appear until 2027.

lanes.source_family: NERC event-analysis reports page and NERC State of Reliability (SOR) page, nerc.com; FERC/NERC joint inquiry and review reports (ferc.gov major-event pages).
lanes.limitation: ferc.gov refused access again (HTTP 403), so FERC's own major-event pages, including any review of the 2026 winter storms, remain unread. NERC has published nothing since 2026-11-03, no event-analysis report on a 2026 event, and no State of Reliability report covering 2026.
lanes.finding: NERC's listing pages render their document lists from links present in the page source; a text-only reader returns an empty page, so the list must be read from the source.

lanes.source_family: DOE CESER emergency situation reports
lanes.limitation: No DOE situation report was released 2026-10-31 to 2026-11-10: the hurricane hub's newest series is still Milton (2024), the extreme-weather hub lists only February 2021, and the CESER news listing shows one item in the window (7 Nov 2026, renewal of two Puerto Rico 202(c) orders: a territory, an order and no reported outage; not a candidate). Marked partial, not enumerated_complete, only because iteration 16 listed but did not open every report of the Ian, Helene and Fiona series; nothing from this pass is unread.
lanes.finding: DOE has published no public situation report for any 2025 or 2026 event, including Isaias 2026; the listing is not a record of DOE responses.

lanes.source_family: NOAA National Hurricane Center Tropical Cyclone Reports (TCRs), read from NHC's own season indexes for the Atlantic and eastern Pacific basins, 2022-2026.
lanes.limitation: NHC has not published reports for Atlantic Dolly, Edouard, Fay, Gonzalo, Hanna, Isaias and Josephine, nor for eastern-Pacific Douglas, Elida, Fausto, Karina, Lowell, Marie and the storms after Norbert. Of the four US-affecting storms that were unpublished on 2026-11-03, one (Arthur) is now out; Edouard, Isaias and Lowell are still unpublished. Josephine (21-22 Oct 2026) was not assessed for US effects because no search could be run.
lanes.finding: The Arthur report documents rain, flooding and tornado damage in Texas, Louisiana and the Southeast but gives no outage count, shut-in volume or facility effect, so it yields no candidate. The execution value restates iteration 17's result in the two-dimension vocabulary.

lanes.source_family: BSEE Gulf storm shut-in statistics releases (bsee.gov newsroom); EIA Today in Energy articles on weather-driven production shut-ins and freeze-offs (eia.gov/tod
lanes.limitation: BSEE's newsroom refused access for the third pass running, so its storm shut-in releases are unenumerated; a release for a smaller storm (Alberto 2024; Arthur, Bertha, Edouard, Josephine 2026) could be missing. The public alternatives opened give no new shut-in event since 2026-11-03 and cannot show that BSEE issued none.
lanes.finding: BSEE's Data Center (data.bsee.gov) answers ordinary requests where the newsroom does not, but it holds no storm statistics. Deriving shut-ins from its monthly production series would be an inference, not a reported effect, and was not attempted.

lanes.source_family: PHMSA pipeline enforcement raw data file (all Corrective Action Order cases)
lanes.limitation: The incident data files, the only complete list of reportable pipeline incidents, are still unread: phmsa.dot.gov refuses the landing pages and the zip, and DOT's open-data portal only links back to them. A trunk-line shutdown that drew neither a corrective action order nor any other enforcement case is therefore invisible to this lane.
lanes.finding: PHMSA publishes no incident CSV, API or bulk file outside phmsa.dot.gov that is reachable by ordinary access. The primis enforcement site does publish an incident-linked case list, and it surfaced trunk-line shutdowns handled by safety order rather than corrective action order, a class the corrective-action-order census cannot see.

lanes.source_family: Per-terminal web query for unplanned LNG export terminal shutdowns
lanes.limitation: Three of nine terminals were searched (Sabine Pass, Cameron, Cove Point); twelve queries for terminals not yet operating in the window were not applicable. The rest were not run because the search limit was reached.
lanes.finding: Cameron, 2022-2026: the ten queries returned planned maintenance (2022, 2024, 2025, 2026) and one January 2024 freeze cargo cancellation with no reported train shutdown. One unverified lead remains: a search summary, with no attributable page, said all three Cameron trains shut unexpectedly on 2025-10-27; it is held, not accepted. Cove Point, 2022-2026: every plant shutdown the 10 queries surfaced is the scheduled autumn maintenance outage (excluded as planned), each year. The only unplanned items are a 14 June 2022 trip recorded in a PHMSA order with no stated effect, and a July 2023 feed gas reduction downstream of the Columbia Line VB rupture already in the corpus. A 2025 PHMSA proposed safety order on minor leaks states no shutdown. Result snippets from RBN and PipeRiv were not opened; RBN weekly reports are subscriber content.

lanes.source_family: CSB investigations list; year-by-year structured web query (refinery and gas-processing shutdowns)
lanes.limitation: The declared set ran through 2026-11-03. An additional 2026 re-check query could not be run in this pass.

lanes.source_family: Year-by-year structured web query for US coal-mine events that cut supply (MSHA and EIA where surfaced)
lanes.limitation: Carried from iteration 17 with no new work: 10 of 10 declared queries, which is a completed query set and not a census. Nothing covers 2026-11-04 to 2026-11-10, and MSHA's mine data retrieval system, the enumerable source for this class, has still not been downloaded or parsed. The execution value is the two-dimension name for iteration 17's '10 of 10'; it is not new coverage.

recovery_by_class.note: Days from the event to the reported recovery, for records where a dated report exists. Fewer than three cases are listed, three or four give a range, five or more a median. These describe what was reported and are not a forecast or a country comparison.
